 KUALA LUMPUR: Telekom Malaysia Bhd 's wholly-owned subsidiary TM Technology Services Sdn Bhd (TM Tech) has received a notification of approval for the Universal Service Plan and designated as the Universal Service Provider (DUSP) for the deployment of network facilities and services for the submarine cable system under the Sambungan Kabel Dasar Laut MADANI (SALAM) (Part 1) project.
 Upon acceptance of the notification, TM Tech would be responsible for the planning, design, engineering, manufacture, supply, delivery, installation, integration, testing, commissioning and completion of the entire Wet Plant and its ancillaries across four submarine cable segments.
 The project has been approved for a maximum cost of RM2.7bil. It is scheduled to commence on Dec 15, 2026, and to be completed in phases by the first quarter of 2030.
 TM said in its filing with Bursa Malaysia it is currently reviewing the terms and conditions of the notification.
 "The notification remains subject to the company's internal review and approval process, as well as the fulfilment of applicable requirements and conditions," it said.
